request: Pull the US high-voltage transmission grid (>=230 kV) from the HIFLD authoritative ArcGIS feed, treat each line as an undirected edge between SUB_1 and SUB_2 substations, and run network analysis: degree / betweenness / eigenvector / pagerank / closeness centrality plus Fruchterman-Reingold layout coordinates seeded by geographic positions. Publish the enriched endpoint table to a new 'Energy Infrastructure' project on Tableau Server so analysts can visualize the network topology in Tableau with x/y coordinates and centrality-driven node attributes.

sources.name: HIFLD US Transmission Backbone
sources.description: HIFLD authoritative US Electric Power Transmission Lines layer, filtered to VOLTAGE>=230 (the high-voltage backbone). One feature per line; SUB_1 and SUB_2 are substation endpoint identifiers. Polyline geometry; we extract first/last vertex into start_lon/start_lat/end_lon/end_lat for the network layout's geographic seed.

args.name: Grid Network Analyzer
args.description: Builds an undirected NetworkX graph from transmission lines keyed by SUB_1 -> SUB_2. Computes Fruchterman-Reingold spring layout (x/y coords) seeded from each substation's geographic mean across all incident edges. Adds node-level metrics: degree_centrality, betweenness_centrality, eigenvector_centrality, pagerank, closeness_centrality. Emits two rows per edge (one per endpoint) so Tableau can render lines via Detail/path-order on edge_id.

outputs.name: US Grid Network (Backbone)
outputs.description: US high-voltage (>=230 kV) electric transmission grid as a network. Each row = one endpoint of one line (two rows per line, joined by edge_id). x/y are Fruchterman-Reingold layout coords for non-geographic 'force-directed' rendering; longitude/latitude are real geographic coords. Node-level centralities (degree / betweenness / eigenvector / pagerank / closeness) attach naturally to node_id. Source: HIFLD authoritative transmission lines layer. Refresh: monthly.
